text.en: You are tonight's moon postman. The last letter has no street number, only: 'To the one still waiting for me to come home.' Dawn is approaching.
text.zh-Hans: 你是今晚的月亮邮差。最后一封信没有门牌，只写着：送给还在等我回家的人。天就快亮了。

text.en: Only a low wall remains of the old street. A cat at its corner chases your shadow. Its brass collar tag bears the name faintly visible inside the envelope.
text.zh-Hans: 旧街只剩一面矮墙，墙角的小猫追着你的影子。它脖子上的铜牌，刻着信封里隐约透出的名字。

text.en: The cat leads you to a new building. An old woman puts a bowl of water outside every day. Since moving, she has feared that her traveler won't find her here.
text.zh-Hans: 小猫带你来到新楼，老人每天都在门口放一碗水。她说，搬家以后，怕远行的人找不到这里。

text.en: When you speak the name, the low wall reflects the old kitchen. A bowl of soup waits on the table. You hear the woman say: 'The address changed. Home is still here.'
text.zh-Hans: 念出名字后，矮墙映出从前的厨房。桌上留着一碗汤，你听见老人说：地址变了，家还在。

text.en: Following the soup's aroma, you enter her new home. She recognizes the handwriting but hesitates to open the letter. 'Will you help me warm the soup first?'
text.zh-Hans: 你循着汤香走进新家，老人认出了信上的字。她迟迟没有拆信，问你能否先陪她把汤热一热？

text.en: A new street number appears on the envelope. The woman waves from her window. There is still time to knock, or you can gently leave the letter on the sill.
text.zh-Hans: 信封上浮现出新的门牌。窗口的老人向你招手，你还来得及敲门，也可以把信轻放在窗台。

text.en: The envelope answers: 'I remember a bowl of hot soup, but not the way.' A cat in the distance suddenly looks up, as though someone has called it.
text.zh-Hans: 信封回答：我记得一碗热汤，却不记得路。远处的小猫突然抬头，像听见有人在叫它。

text.en: The cat leads you to a new building. An old woman puts a bowl of water outside every day. Since moving, she has feared that her traveler won't find her here.
text.zh-Hans: 小猫带你来到新楼，老人每天都在门口放一碗水。她说，搬家以后，怕远行的人找不到这里。

text.en: When you speak the name, the low wall reflects the old kitchen. A bowl of soup waits on the table. You hear the woman say: 'The address changed. Home is still here.'
text.zh-Hans: 念出名字后，矮墙映出从前的厨房。桌上留着一碗汤，你听见老人说：地址变了，家还在。

text.en: The envelope that talked with you along the way admits it fears being finished and forgotten. The woman will keep it for company, or let you take it on more deliveries.
text.zh-Hans: 一路与你说话的信封终于承认，它也害怕被读完。老人愿意把它留下作伴，或让你带它继续送信。

text.en: The envelope gives you the new address but hates to say goodbye. After reading the letter, the woman asks you to show it more homes, or leave it by her window for company.
text.zh-Hans: 信封把新门牌告诉你，却舍不得告别。老人读完信，问你能否带它看更多的家，或留在窗边陪她。

text.en: Only after sharing the hot soup does she slowly unfold the letter. Before dawn, you finally understand that a postman delivers more than messages on paper.
text.zh-Hans: 你陪老人喝完热汤，她才慢慢展开信。天亮前，你终于懂得，邮差送到的不只是纸上的消息。

text.en: Morning lights the new address on the envelope. After reading the letter, she polishes her door number until it shines. Her traveler will never mistake the way home again.
text.zh-Hans: 晨光照亮信封上的新地址。老人读完信，把门牌擦得很亮。从此远行的人，再也不会找错家。

text.en: From the start, you listened to the letter's wishes. The woman keeps it by her window and talks with it each night. Messages from far away now have an answering voice.
text.zh-Hans: 你从一开始就听见了信的心事。老人把它留在窗边，每晚和它说说话，远行的消息有了回声。

text.en: The woman keeps the letter and gives you the talking envelope. The next night it sits in your postbag, remembering every light that welcomes someone home.
text.zh-Hans: 老人留下信纸，将会说话的信封交给你。下个夜晚，它坐在你的邮袋里，替你记住每一盏归家的灯。

summary.en: Tonight's last letter is addressed to a home that no longer stands.
summary.zh-Hans: 今晚最后一封信，收件地址是已经拆掉的家。
